From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-demo: private connectivity + embeddings/rerank integration

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can unblock the POC. TL;DR: Redwood can support a private VPC endpoint + IP allowlist for low-latency inference, and we recommend using our embeddings + reranker pipeline for the relevance use case you demoed.

Key technical assumptions (please confirm):
- POC will run against your staging VPC in us-west-2.
- You want inference traffic over a private VPC endpoint (AWS PrivateLink or VPC Endpoint) to avoid public egress.
- Requests will come from your app servers and an async batch job for offline embedding refresh.

Open architecture items we discussed:
1) Network: VPC endpoint vs NAT egress + IP allowlist. We typically recommend VPC endpoint for stable private connectivity; fallback to IP allowlist if LB/NAT integration is simpler for you.
2) Auth: SDK + service account keys (short-lived JWTs) for server-to-server auth. We can support mTLS for stricter setups — see Qs below.
3) Routing: Route inference traffic to a pinned model variant in Dedicated mode for predictable latency; we can also set up automatic fallback to a lower-cost variant if capacity constrained.
4) Features: embeddings, reranker, structured-tool-calling responses (we can return JSON schema for your search API to parse).

Requested action items / next steps:
- Alex: share contact for your infra/networking lead and preferred s3 or drive folder for config exchange (we'll share a sample network diagram and SDK sample).
- Priya: confirm expected queries per second and typical sequence lengths for reranker. This will inform batching/kv cache sizing.
- Stephanie (cc): prepare a short POC checklist (network requirements, required ports, cert types) so we can schedule a 1-hr network sync next week.

Attachments: we'll upload a simple network-diagram.pdf and a sample-sdk-config.yaml with auth snippets + sample cURL.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes

Subject: Re: Post-demo: private connectivity + embeddings/rerank integration — technical checklist

Alex / team — attaching a couple of artifacts to make the network sync efficient: network-diagram.pdf (simple reference architecture showing PrivateLink + routing) and sample-sdk-config.yaml (server auth, example call patterns for embeddings + reranker).

A few technical notes from ops: 
- Ports: outbound 443 only from your app servers if using VPC endpoint. If IP allowlist: you'll need outbound NAT to our public IP ranges (we'll provide a CIDR list).
- DNS: For PrivateLink we recommend you create a private hosted zone that points the model-api.redwood.internal name to the endpoint ENI. We can provide the CNAME we use.
- mTLS: Redwood supports two modes:
  * Managed mTLS (we handle cert rotation) — requires you to add our root CA to the endpoint allowlist.
  * Customer-provided certs — you upload a PEM bundle to our console; we accept x509 chains signed by public or private CAs.
- API auth: short-lived JWTs issued via an internal service account; sample flow in sample-sdk-config.yaml. If you prefer API keys we can provision scoped keys but they are long-lived and not recommended for production.

On the inference side (embeddings + reranker):
- For interactive search, we recommend an embeddings index (periodic batch embedding refresh) + a small neural reranker for the top-K. Expect throughput ~ 0.5–2x of raw embedding QPS depending on reranker size.
- We'll need a small labeled set (~200 examples) to tune reranker precision — Priya noted you have in-house relevance labels; can we get a secure link to a sanitized subset?

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) network-team: create the endpoint and share the endpoint-id + security group details (we'll provide security group example).
2) Priya: share QPS and a sample of relevance labels in the shared drive folder.
3) Redwood: we'll prepare a POC runbook (network steps, sample calls, expected metrics) and book a 1-hr kickoff (propose Tue 2027-05-11 09:00 PT).

Thanks — Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
